# Signal OS - Incident Response Framework

**Generated by:** incident-review-guide skill
**Version:** 1.0
**Classification:** Internal - Signal OS Engineering

---

## 1. Incident Severity Classification

| Level | Name | Definition | Response Time | Examples |
|-------|------|-----------|---------------|----------|
| **P0** | Critical | Complete service outage or data breach | 5 minutes | All scoring APIs down, database failure, security breach |
| **P1** | High | Major feature degradation | 15 minutes | Scoring latency >10s, auth failure, >50% error rate |
| **P2** | Medium | Partial feature impairment | 1 hour | Trend forecasting offline, reporting delays, UI bugs |
| **P3** | Low | Minor issue, workaround available | 4 hours | Display glitches, non-critical feature unavailable |

---

## 2. Incident Response Team (IRT)

| Role | Responsibility | Primary | Backup |
|------|---------------|---------|--------|
| Incident Commander | Coordinates response, makes decisions | Lead Engineer | CTO |
| Communications Lead | Internal/external communication | Head of Growth | CEO |
| Technical Lead | Root cause analysis and fix | Senior Backend | Senior Frontend |
| SRE Lead | Infrastructure and monitoring | DevOps Engineer | Cloud Architect |

---

## 3. Response Playbooks

### 3.1 P0: Complete Service Outage

```
T+0min    ALERT    PagerDuty alerts on-call engineer
T+5min    ACK      On-call acknowledges, assesses scope
T+10min   PAGE    If unresolved, page Incident Commander
T+15min   WAR ROOM  Bridge call initiated, IRT assembled
T+30min   MITIGATE  Temporary fix or rollback deployed
T+1hr     UPDATE   Customer communication sent
T+2hr     RESOLVE  Service fully restored
T+24hr    POSTMORTEM Postmortem document drafted
T+72hr    REVIEW   Postmortem reviewed, action items assigned
```

### 3.2 P1: Scoring Engine Degradation

**Detection:** p99 scoring latency >10s OR error rate >50%

**Immediate Actions:**
1. Check scoring service health in dashboard
2. If single region: fail over to secondary region
3. If model issue: rollback to previous model version
4. If queue backup: scale workers horizontally
5. Notify customers via status page

**Rollback Procedures:**
```bash
# Scoring engine rollback
kubectl rollout undo deployment/scoring-engine -n production

# Model rollback
aws s3 cp s3://models/previous/ s3://models/current/ --recursive
kubectl rollout restart deployment/scoring-engine -n production

# Database failover
# Automatic - RDS Multi-AZ handles this
```

### 3.3 P0: Data Breach / Security Incident

**Immediate Actions:**
1. Contain: Isolate affected systems
2. Assess: Determine scope of data exposure
3. Notify: Legal team within 1 hour
4. Document: Preserve all logs and evidence
5. Engage: External forensics if needed

**Notification Requirements:**
| Jurisdiction | Timeline | Authority |
|-------------|----------|-----------|
| GDPR (EU) | 72 hours | Supervisory Authority |
| CCPA (California) | Without unreasonable delay | CA Attorney General |
| PIPL (China) | Immediate | CAC |
| Users | Without delay | Direct notification |

## 4. Communication Templates

### 4.1 Internal Slack Alert

```
:rotating_light: INCIDENT ALERT - P{severity}
Service: {affected_service}
Impact: {description}
Started: {timestamp}
Commander: {incident_commander}
Bridge: {war_room_link}
Status: {investigating/mitigated/resolved}
```

### 4.2 Status Page Update

**Investigating:**
> We are currently investigating reports of {issue}. Some users may experience {symptom}. We will provide updates as more information becomes available.

**Identified:**
> We have identified the cause of {issue}. Our team is actively working on a fix. We expect resolution within {ETA}.

**Monitoring:**
> A fix has been deployed and we are monitoring the situation. Services should be returning to normal. We will update once we confirm full recovery.

**Resolved:**
> The issue has been resolved. All services are operating normally. A postmortem will be published within 24 hours.

### 4.3 Customer Email (P0/P1 only)

```
Subject: Signal OS Service Update - Issue Resolved

Hi {name},

We experienced a service disruption today from {start_time} to {end_time} 
that affected {impact_description}.

What happened:
{brief_description}

What we did:
{resolution_summary}

What's next:
We are conducting a full postmortem analysis. You can track our progress 
at https://status.signal-os.app/incidents/{incident_id}

We apologize for any inconvenience this may have caused.

— Signal OS Engineering Team
```

## 5. Postmortem Template

```markdown
# Postmortem: [Incident Title]

## Metadata
- Incident ID: INC-YYYY-MM-NNN
- Severity: P{0-3}
- Date: YYYY-MM-DD
- Duration: HH:MM
- Reporter: {name}
- Reviewers: {names}

## Summary
[1-2 sentence summary of what happened and impact]

## Timeline
| Time (UTC) | Event | Category |
|-----------|-------|----------|
| HH:MM | Event description | TRIGGER/DETECT/ACTION/RESOLVE/INFO |

## Root Cause Analysis (5 Whys)
1. Why? → [Answer]
2. Why? → [Answer]
3. Why? → [Answer]
4. Why? → [Answer]
5. Why? → [Root Cause]

## Impact
- Affected users: {count} ({percentage}%)
- Features affected: {list}
- Data impact: {none/partial/full description}
- Financial impact: {if applicable}

## What Went Well
1. {positive item}

## What Went Wrong
1. {negative item}

## Action Items
| Priority | Action | Owner | Due Date | Type |
|----------|--------|-------|----------|------|
| P0 | {action} | {owner} | {date} | mitigate/detect/prevent/process |

## Lessons Learned
- {key takeaway}
```

---

## 6. Blameless Culture Checklist

All incident documents MUST pass this check:

| Check | Pass Criteria |
|-------|--------------|
| No individual names as causes | Use "the process" or "the system" |
| No "should have" language | Use "the process did not include" |
| Focus on system improvement | Every finding has an action item |
| Facts only in timeline | No speculation, only observed events |
| Constructive tone | Forward-looking, not blame-assigning |

---

## 7. Escalation Matrix

| Time Elapsed | Escalation Action |
|-------------|-------------------|
| 5 min (P0) / 15 min (P1) | On-call → Incident Commander |
| 30 min | Incident Commander → VP Engineering |
| 1 hour | VP Engineering → CTO |
| 2 hours | CTO → CEO + Board notification (P0 only) |
| 4 hours (P0) | External crisis PR engaged |
